title: Decentralized, Epoch-based F2FS Journaling with Fine-grained Crash Recovery
problem: Flash-friendly file systems (F2FS) require efficient journaling mechanisms; centralized journaling creates bottlenecks and limits scalability in multi-threaded or distributed scenarios.
motivation: Decentralized journaling improves scalability and concurrency in file systems while maintaining crash consistency.
method: Instead of funneling all file system changes through a single journal (creating a bottleneck), this spreads the journaling across multiple independent journals organized by epochs—fixed time windows. When a crash occurs, the system recovers individual transactions within epochs rather than replaying entire epochs. This lets multiple processes simultaneously write to different journals without queuing at a central point, improving performance on multi-core systems.
key_novelty: The core innovation is decentralized journaling organized into epochs (time windows) with fine-grained recovery, enabling concurrent writes without central bottlenecking.
limitations: Complexity of managing decentralized state; validation under high concurrency and crash scenarios needed.
